note: Ratings for the blinded adapter-fidelity package, unblinded against the sealed key. The key's sha256 matches the value recorded in adapter_listening.json before rating, so these were made blind.
rater: the project owner, not a naive listener

registered_prediction.large_gap_sets: the shipped arm is chosen clearly and consistently (ECAPA gap +0.315)
registered_prediction.no_gap_sets: near chance (ECAPA gap +0.017 - the metric says there is nothing to hear)
registered_prediction.controls: the foreign narrator is rejected in all 3; if not, nothing else in this package is readable
registered_prediction.falsifies_ecapa_if: both classes come out near chance, which would mean the metric does not track audible speaker identity at this scale

verdict: HELD. Where ECAPA reports a 0.315 gap the rater chose the higher-scoring arm 4 of 4, on identical sentences with the arms shuffled between slots. Where it reports -0.017 the rater could not tell in half the sets and never preferred the other arm. ECAPA tracks an audible difference at this scale.
controls_are_compromised: The three controls paired the reference against a foreign narrator reading a DIFFERENT sentence, because the builder took clip <index> from that adapter's own holdout. The rater identified all three unprompted as mismatched. 3-of-3 therefore shows that a mismatch is noticeable, not that speaker identity is audible, and must not be quoted as a passed control. The eight test sets are unaffected - same line, same holdout, only the arm differs - which is also why they cannot be answered from content.
limitations: Two adapters, one narrator each, twelve lines drawn from one held-out set - this asks whether the metric tracks anything audible, not how well.
The rater is expected to be the project owner, who is not a naive listener; goal 7.1 records that limitation already.
'same' answers are counted separately and are not evidence for either arm.
One rater, one session, eight scoreable sets.
Two adapters. This asks whether the metric tracks anything audible, not how well it tracks.
The controls are void; the package has no passing positive control.
